message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p4 in a 1v1 against p3. I just paid $4 rent to them and have $321 cash. I own 10 properties total: MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, NEW_YORK_AVENUE, and three others are mortgaged. I also have one house on each of ATLANTIC_AVENUE, VENTNOR_AVENUE, and MARVIN_GARDENS.

I also own PARK_PLACE and BOARDWALK, and I have two get-out-of-jail cards.

p3 has $931 cash. They are on the JAIL space but not in jail. They own all four railroads, a light blue monopoly with hotels, a pink monopoly with hotels, a green monopoly with hotels, and SHORT_LINE. I have the other two red properties mortgaged.

I can liquidate my holdings for roughly $676 total. That is still far below the $1,275 rent on a green hotel. I am calculating whether I can survive that hit.

Green hotels now cost $1,275 on Pacific and NC, and $1,400 on Penn. Light blue hotels are $550–$600, pink are $750–$900, and railroads are $200. I am on Baltic Avenue and must choose an action before rolling next turn.

I am mapping the board from Baltic Avenue to identify every possible landing spot and its rent. Rolling 2–4 lands on light blue hotels, 5–7 on pink hotels, 8 on the Pennsylvania RR, and 9–10 on my mortgaged properties. I am checking whether a double roll could also hit Community Chest.

I mapped the exact rent for every possible roll from Baltic Avenue. Rolling 2 lands on Reading Railroad for $200, 3 on Oriental hotel for $550, 4 on Vermont hotel for $550, 5 on Connecticut hotel for $600, 6 on Jail for $0, 7 on St. Charles hotel for $750, 8 on Electric Company for $0, 9 on States hotel for $750, 10 on Virginia hotel for $900, 11 on Pennsylvania RR for $200, and 12 on St. James Place for $0.

I calculated the probability of each roll. Eleven of thirty-six rolls are safe. Three are cheap. Thirteen are deadly.

Rolls 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10 cost $550 to $900. I can cover the first two with full liquidation. The last four are instant death.

Rolls 2 and 11 land on railroads for $200. That is manageable.

Liquidating before the roll cannot save me from unaffordable rent. The engine only allows mortgaging and selling when I actually owe money. Pre-liquidating is pointless for survival.

I am now considering building more houses on my yellow properties. Each house costs $150. I have one house on each yellow street. I must build evenly.

I cannot afford to build three houses on my yellow properties. Even one house would cost $150 and leave me with only $171 cash.

The rent from two houses on any single yellow street is still well below p3's $931. Building more houses on my yellows will not threaten them enough to matter.

I cannot afford to build three houses on my yellows. That would cost $900, and even two houses would cost $450.

Selling my houses would give me cash but destroy my only weapon, and rebuilding would be difficult.

I can unmortgage Park Place for about $193, which I can afford. Boardwalk is too expensive at roughly $220.

Unmortgaging only Park Place would be useless because mortgaged properties do not collect rent. Unmortgaging both St. James and Tennessee for $198 would complete the orange monopoly and leave $123 cash. Orange rents without houses are only $14–$16, but with houses they rise to $70–$220.

Unmortgaging both St. James and Tennessee would leave only $23 after building one house, so the orange rent would still be too low to threaten p3.

Trading is also unwise. If I gave p3 the red properties, they would complete a red monopoly with hotels costing over $1,000 each. If I traded Mediterranean Avenue for Baltic, they would own the brown monopoly.

Neither player currently owns a brown monopoly, so trading Mediterranean Avenue would not give p3 a free brown hotel. They would likely demand something valuable in return, such as a railroad or Illinois Avenue, but that exchange is unappealing because I have no railroads and Illinois alone pays only $20 in rent.

I have two get-out-of-jail-free cards. I will keep them as a safety net and avoid building, unmortgaging, or trading to preserve cash for survivable rolls.

I am now considering whether p3 can land on my yellow properties from Jail. I have ruled out any trade proposals because they would not give me greens, pinks, or light blues in return.

p3 cannot land on my yellow properties from Jail this turn. Atlantic, Ventnor, and Marvin are too far away to reach in one roll.

I will roll from Baltic into their death zone next turn. I expect to hit a hotel 22 times out of 36. Thirteen of those hits cost $750 or more, which would bankrupt me even after full liquidation.

I am now calculating exact survival probabilities for this roll. Thirteen of thirty-six outcomes are instant death. Nine are survivable hotels that would leave me with roughly seventy-six to one hundred twenty-six dollars after full liquidation. Three are safe rolls, and three are railroads costing two hundred dollars.

I am now considering a desperate trade proposal. I would offer p3 my entire yellow monopoly, orange properties, dark blue holdings, Mediterranean Avenue, utilities, both get-out-of-jail-free cards, and all remaining cash in exchange for something valuable.

I realized that breaking p3's green monopoly would force them to sell their hotels back to the bank. That would instantly wipe out their biggest income source and turn the game around. I am now weighing whether I can trick them into trading a green property for my entire empire.

Trading a property from a monopoly with buildings requires selling the hotels first, so the engine might reject the offer. Even then, p3 would not accept a green hotel for my entire portfolio because it would not threaten them. I also realized that unmortgaging my red properties would complete a red monopoly.

Unmortgaging both Kentucky and Indiana would cost $242, leaving only $79. I cannot complete a red monopoly because p3 already owns Illinois. Trading for Illinois would give them the red set while I receive just $20 in rent. I am now considering offering cash for that property.

I realized that if I go bankrupt to p3, they inherit all my properties automatically. They have no incentive to trade me anything useful now. I will simply end my turn.

I considered mortgaging Mediterranean Avenue and New York to raise cash, but realized the engine only allows mortgaging when I actually owe money, so doing it now would be pointless. I also checked whether p3 could land on New York from Jail this turn; that roll is nine spaces away, which is too far to reach.

I checked whether p3 could land on New York from Jail. That roll would require passing GO, which is impossible from position 10.

I also calculated the exact cash shortfall for a $550 hit. I would need to mortgage Mediterranean Avenue and New York, then sell both houses to survive. That leaves me with only one house and almost no cash.

Pre-building would reduce my available cash even more, so I will not build or sell houses.
